title: Banana Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Banana Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Banana nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of potassium, nitrogen and magnesium in saging, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Banana nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your saging (banana) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are potassium, nitrogen, magnesium, zinc, boron, calcium, phosphorus, sulfur, manganese and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Young banana plants whose older leaves have turned yellow with brown dead edges from potassium shortage
heroImage.credit: Zhang et al., PLOS Pathogens 2025, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Potassium, nitrogen, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron, calcium, sulfur, manganese and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which banana nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a banana nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest banana nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Potassium deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Young banana plants whose older leaves have turned yellow with brown dead edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Zhang et al., PLOS Pathogens 2025, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: The oldest leaves yellow first, starting at the leaf tip and between the veins. The yellow turns orange, the patches join, and the tissue dries dark brown, often as a scorch along the edges. Leaves get smaller, may split along the side veins, and the midrib can bend and break. Bunches come late and stay short and thin, with small fingers that fill poorly. You see it most at this stage: any age, but worst from the fast leaf growth stage to bunch filling, when the plant takes up the most potash.
Why potassium deficiency happens in saging
Sandy or light soils, acid soils and heavy rain that washes potash away. Soils already rich in magnesium, which hold back potash uptake. Long dry spells also cut uptake.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves. But the yellow band sits between the midrib and the edge while the edge stays green. To be sure, send a leaf sample and a soil sample to a lab. A soil test that shows low potash, or a high magnesium to potash balance, points to this. Bunches that fill better after potash is added confirm it.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil around the mat, split into several doses, following the soil test. While the soil dose takes effect, spray the leaves with Sulfate of potash at 1 percent (10 grams per liter, 160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Keep the soil pH above 6 with lime or dolomite on acid soils. Give 200 to 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 a mat every two to three months, more as the bunch forms.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.

To keep it away, give potash every cycle, in splits, from the early vegetative stage up to bunch emergence. Return chopped leaves and pseudostems to the mat. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Nitrogen deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Row of young banana plants with pale, yellow green leaves from a mild nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The oldest leaves go light green, then yellow, and the veins do not stay green. Leaf stalks, midribs and leaf sheaths take on a pink to reddish color. The pseudostem stays thin, new leaves are small and come slowly, and leaves may crowd together. Bunch weight and fruit quality drop. You see it most at this stage: from early growth to bunch emergence, most often in fast growing young plants.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in saging

Sandy soils with little organic matter, heavy rain or irrigation that washes nitrogen down. Fresh straw or raw manure that ties up nitrogen as it rots. Roots damaged by nematodes or weevils also take up less.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency also gives light green to yellow leaves, but it starts on the young leaves. Iron deficiency starts on young leaves and keeps the midrib and veins green for a while. To be sure, A leaf test shows low nitrogen. Check that the roots are healthy. New leaves that green up within a few weeks after urea confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 around the mat and water it in. Give 300 grams of Urea per plant, then irrigate. Split it into smaller doses on sandy soil. Add compost or well rotted manure to build the soil.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Ammonium Chloride** by La Filipina (25 0 0), **Hyfer Urea Max (Locally Blended Coated)** by Agrotiger (44 0 0) and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, split nitrogen through the crop, from the third month up to bunch emergence. Keep a mulch of old leaves on the mat. Let a soil test and the crop's color set the season's nitrogen.
Magnesium deficiency in banana

Old leaves yellow in the middle part of the blade, along the midrib, while the leaf edge stays green. Dead spots form inside the yellow parts. The leaf stalk shows bluish purple mottling, and leaf sheaths may pull away from the pseudostem. Bunch weight and yield fall. You see it most at this stage: mostly on older plants and after heavy potash feeding, during the vegetative stage and bunch filling.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in saging

Sandy and acid soils, and heavy use of potash, which competes with magnesium. Cold, wet spells make it worse. The opposite also happens on some plantations: soil very high in magnesium crowds out potash and calcium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also hits old leaves, but it starts at the tip and edge as an orange scorch. Manganese deficiency looks similar but starts on young leaves. To be sure, do a soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together, since the balance matters, and a leaf test. Purple mottled leaf stalks with green leaf edges are a strong field sign.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Apply Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) or Kieserite around the mat and water it in. Give 25 grams of Magnesium sulfate per plant. On acid soils use Dolomite, which gives both lime and magnesium. Do not put magnesium and potash fertilizer down on the same day. Put the soil dose in before planting or when the rains begin. Sprays show results in 10 to 14 days.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **Magnesium Sulphate Anhydrous** by Newman Chemicals (20 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, base potash and magnesium on a soil test so one does not crowd out the other. Use dolomite instead of plain lime on acid soils.
Zinc deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Banana leaf with pale yellow stripes between the green veins from zinc shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Sunitha et al., Data in Brief 2023, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: Young leaves come out smaller and more lance shaped, with yellow to white stripes between the side veins that give a striped, mottled look. The underside of the rolled new leaf shows a strong purple tint. Leaves may crowd into a rosette. Bunches are small and the fingers short, thin, twisted and light green at the tip. You see it most at this stage: on young plants and suckers, and in later cycles. Losses often show in the second or third year.
Why zinc deficiency happens in saging
High pH or limed soils, organic soils, heavy phosphorus fertilizer, and cold wet weather. It is the most common micronutrient shortage in banana.
How to tell it apart

Bunchy top virus also gives narrow, bunched leaves. But it shows dark green dot and dash streaks along the veins and leaf stalk and the leaves stand stiff and upright. To be sure, A leaf test for zinc and a soil test for pH and phosphorus. Spray a few plants with zinc sulfate. New leaves that come out normal confirm it.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray Zinc sulfate on the leaves. Use 5 grams per liter (80 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) (0.5 percent), or 2 grams per liter (32 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) plus 2.5 grams of lime per liter on young leaves. On poor soils also apply Zinc sulfate to the soil, following the soil test. Do not apply it on the same day as phosphate fertilizer. A usual soil dose is 20 to 25 kg of Zinc sulfate per hectare (about 5 kg of zinc), mixed with the basal fertilizer. It lasts two or three crops.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc), **Liquid Chelate Zinc with Sulfur** by Sagrex (10 percent zinc and 5 percent sulfur) and **Nemes Foliar** by SCL Filipinas (4.8 0 0 with 10 percent zinc, 4.9 percent boron and 4.8 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming and very heavy phosphorus. Include zinc in the program on soils that tested low.
Boron deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Banana leaf with a crinkled, rippled blade, a boron shortage sign
blocks.caption: Photo: Forest and Kim Starr, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The youngest leaves show it. Leaf edges go pale and curl inward, then brown. White streaks run across the veins on the underside, the side veins thicken, and the blade can be crumpled, misshapen or missing. Plants may be stunted with leaves bunched in a fan. Bunches are light, poorly filled or deformed. You see it most at this stage: during fast leaf growth and around flowering, often after a dry spell.
Why boron deficiency happens in saging
Sandy or alkaline soils low in organic matter, drought, and very high nitrogen or calcium. Cold wet spells can also bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Calcium deficiency also damages young leaves, but its dead tissue is lighter brown and starts at the tip. The side veins thicken more. To be sure, A leaf test for boron, and a soil test. New leaves that come out normal after a light boron dose confirm it. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Apply Borax to the soil around the root zone. Give 25 grams per plant. A foliar spray of Borax at 1 gram per liter (16 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) also works. Boron is toxic in excess, so do not repeat high doses without a test. Give boron before flowering: flowers and fruit set need it most.

Sold here with boron: **Borax Decahydrate** by Parafield (10.5 percent boron), **Etifert 15 (Borax Pentahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (15 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up and water during dry spells. Add a small boron dose on soils that tested low. Test the soil every two or three years.
Calcium deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Banana plant whose youngest leaf is curled and bent over, a calcium shortage sign
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Young leaves fail to open fully, giving a 'spike leaf' with a deformed or missing blade. Leaves pale, then die back light brown from the tip, with thick side veins. Roots are short and thick. The peel splits as fruit ripens, fingers curl, and weak fruit tips let cigar end rot in. You see it most at this stage: during fast growth and fruit formation.
Why calcium deficiency happens in saging
Acid soils, sandy soils that leach, soils high in sodium or aluminum, drought, and heavy potash or nitrogen that pushes calcium out.
How to tell it apart

Boron deficiency also hurts young leaves, but its dead tissue is darker and starts at the leaf edge with white streaks under the leaf. Virus and herbicide damage can also deform new leaves. To be sure, soil test for pH and calcium, and a leaf test. Low pH with spike leaves points to calcium.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soils apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite to the mat, following the soil test. Rates run from 50 grams to 1 kg of lime per plant, split over the year. On soils with normal pH use Gypsum or Calcium nitrate. Do not overload potash.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** (36.2 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium) and **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils before planting, keep water steady, and keep potash and calcium in balance.
Phosphorus deficiency in banana

Growth is slow and the plant stays short, with a thin, woody pseudostem and weak roots. The edges of old leaves yellow in a saw tooth pattern with purplish brown flecks, then die, and the leaves curl. Leaf stalks break easily. Young leaves look dark bluish green, sometimes purple underneath. You see it most at this stage: early growth, right after planting and in young suckers.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in saging
Acid soils that lock up phosphorus, very alkaline soils, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soil, and poor roots.
How to tell it apart

Too much nitrogen also gives dark blue green leaves. Manganese deficiency also kills leaf edges, but its dead areas are darker and it starts on younger leaves. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer near the roots and water it in. Give 50 grams of DAP (Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0) per plant. On acid soils correct the pH with lime so the phosphorus stays available. Give it at planting and every three months.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole and in the first months, and lime acid soils. Test the soil every two or three years.
Sulfur deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Young banana leaf evenly pale yellow, veins included, from sulphur shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Sunitha et al., Data in Brief 2023, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: Young leaves turn light green to yellowish white, evenly over the whole leaf, veins included. New leaves are small and the side veins can look thick, and in bad cases the edges die. The plant grows slowly and bunches stay small or get stuck in the throat. You see it most at this stage: during fast vegetative growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in saging
Acid, sandy soils that leach, low organic matter, waterlogged soils. Years of using only urea and muriate of potash with no sulfur.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen deficiency looks the same but starts on old leaves. Iron deficiency also hits young leaves, but it is patchy and keeps green areas near the midrib. To be sure, leaf test for sulfur and a soil test. Plants that green up after a sulfur fertilizer confirm it. In a soil test, less than 10 ppm of sulfate sulfur is low.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use a nitrogen or phosphorus fertilizer that carries sulfur, such as Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or 16 20 0, in place of part of the urea. Give 20 grams per plant of a complex fertilizer that carries sulfur. Gypsum also supplies sulfur. Give it at planting or with the first side dress.

Sold here with sulfur: **Atlas Ammosul 21 0 0** by Atlas Fertilizer (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Philphos Gypsum** (22.2 percent calcium and 17.4 percent sulfur), **Harvester Sulphate of Potash** by Universal Harvester (0 0 50 with 17.5 percent sulfur) and **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use ammonium sulfate or 16 20 0 for part of the nitrogen every cycle. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Manganese deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Banana leaf with yellow and green streaks running from the midrib out to the edge, like comb teeth, from manganese shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Sunitha et al., Data in Brief 2023, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: It shows first on the second or third youngest leaf. Mild cases are just light green. Then yellow starts at the leaf edge and runs in along the veins toward the midrib, giving a comb tooth pattern. In bad cases the yellow areas die and the edges curl down. You see it most at this stage: during fast growth, more often in cool wet months.
Why manganese deficiency happens in saging
High pH or limed soils, sandy soils, organic soils, and cold wet periods.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency looks similar but starts on old leaves. Iron deficiency yellows the whole young leaf without the comb tooth pattern or dead areas. To be sure, leaf test for manganese and soil test for pH. Test spray a few plants. In a soil test, less than 1 ppm of manganese is low.
What to apply for manganese deficiency

Spray Manganese sulfate on the leaves at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter, 80 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Repeat if new leaves still show it. Spray the young leaves in the cool of the day, soon after sunrise or near sunset.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl Chem (31 percent manganese), **Tierramino MN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 12 percent manganese), **Multimate** by Agway (4 0 0 with 4.5 percent sulfur, 2.8 percent zinc and 1.8 percent manganese) and **Nutri Tabble Meta Foliar** by NS Northern Organic Fertilizer (12 percent zinc, 9 percent sulfur, 2 percent magnesium and 1.2 percent manganese). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming. On high pH soils include manganese in the foliar program. Test the soil every two or three years.
Iron deficiency in banana

blocks.alt: Banana leaf turned almost wholly yellow with a pale midrib from iron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Sunitha et al., Data in Brief 2023, CC BY 4.0, via the publisher

blocks.text: Young leaves turn yellowish green, then yellow or nearly white. The yellow starts between the veins near the base and edges and spreads to the tip, giving a mottled look. The midrib and veins stay green longer but fade in bad cases. Growth slows and bunches stay small. You see it most at this stage: young plants and new leaves, especially after flooding.
Why iron deficiency happens in saging
High pH and limey soils, waterlogged soils, and too much copper, manganese or zinc.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency also yellows young leaves, but evenly with no green veins. Nitrogen deficiency starts on old leaves. To be sure, soil test for pH and check drainage. A test spray of iron on a few plants that greens the new leaves confirms it. Leaf iron numbers alone are not reliable.
What to apply for iron deficiency

Spray Ferrous sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter, 80 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) mixed with Urea at 1 percent (10 grams per liter, 160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Improve drainage where water stands. Spray the young leaves in the cool of the day, soon after sunrise or near sunset.

Sold here with iron: **DDDD Planter's Choice Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Modern Time (19 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl Chem (30 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulphate Monohydrate** by Newman Chemicals (30 percent iron) and **Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, drain wet spots and avoid overliming. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any banana nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your saging needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Banana nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my saging leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is potassium deficiency: old leaves turn orange yellow from the tip, the edges scorch brown and the midrib bends. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in banana?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil around the mat, split into several doses, following the soil test. While the soil dose takes effect, spray the leaves with Sulfate of potash at 1 percent (10 grams per liter, 160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in banana?
items.a: Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 around the mat and water it in. Give 300 grams of Urea per plant, then irrigate.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in banana?
items.a: Apply Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) or Kieserite around the mat and water it in. Give 25 grams of Magnesium sulfate per plant.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my saging lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the banana nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
